Firefighters Learn The Hard Way That Putting Water On A Magnesium Fire Is A Terrible Idea
39 mins ago
Audio By Carbonatix
A massive two-alarm fire engulfed and destroyed the Chicago Magnesium Casting Company plant in Dixmoor earlier this year.
The plant was closed when the fire broke out at 141st Street and Seeley Avenue, CBS Chicago reports. The plant manufactures aircraft components.
Because water or foam causes explosions if applied to magnesium fires, the plant fire was a challenge. Firefighters trained hoses on areas thought to have no magnesium in them, to cool them, while the magnesium burned itself out. Nevertheless, there were several explosions during the course of the fire.
The fire ultimately caused the roof of the plant to collapse. No one was injured in the fire and the cause is being investigated.
